assessment.nobel_worthiness: A transformative empirical programme making intergenerational mobility measurable at population scale and central to economics.
assessment.attribution: Chetty, Hendren and Friedman are a coherent core for the administrative-data measurement and analysis contribution.
assessment.maturity: The agenda has produced a sustained body of influential evidence and research infrastructure.
uncertainties: The appropriate boundary between the measurement programme and its many related collaborators remains difficult to draw.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their work reshaped understanding of how technology, tasks and trade shocks alter local labour demand and inequality.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn and Hanson form a clear core spanning task-based change and the empirical analysis of trade exposure.
assessment.maturity: The contribution is well developed, consequential and has generated a large subsequent literature.
uncertainties: The broad empirical literature makes a single unifying discovery harder to delimit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The monopsony framework has fundamentally changed analysis of wage setting, employer power and labour-market policy.
assessment.attribution: Manning is the central theoretical architect, while Naidu is an important contributor to the modern empirical and institutional programme.
assessment.maturity: The once-marginal framework is now broadly integrated into labour economics and policy analysis.
uncertainties: Assigning credit across foundational theory and the later empirical revival requires care.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This research established early-life conditions and skill formation as central mechanisms for lifetime inequality and human capital.
assessment.attribution: Currie, Almond and Cunha represent complementary empirical and dynamic conceptual contributions.
assessment.maturity: The evidence base is extensive and the ideas have shaped research across health, education and labour economics.
uncertainties: The contribution combines several related mechanisms rather than one narrowly bounded discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Partial identification supplied a principled way to make credible inference when conventional assumptions cannot be defended.
assessment.attribution: Manski is foundational, with Tamer and Molinari central to the development of moment-inequality methods and applications.
assessment.maturity: The approach is mature, widely used and especially important for transparent empirical work under limited information.
uncertainties: The intellectual roots and applications extend beyond the three-person allocation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Audit and correspondence studies made discrimination measurable in real labour markets and changed the evidentiary standard for the field.
assessment.attribution: Bertrand and Mullainathan are central to the canonical audit-study contribution; Charles is a major contributor to the broader labour-market discrimination agenda.
assessment.maturity: The designs have been replicated, extended and influential in scholarship and public debate.
uncertainties: The method has a longer and broader history than the proposed trio.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The work joined theory and measurement to clarify adverse selection in insurance markets and the limits of market design.
assessment.attribution: Finkelstein, Einav and Salanie offer a coherent allocation across empirical measurement and theoretical interpretation.
assessment.maturity: The contribution has generated a durable empirical insurance-economics literature.
uncertainties: The extent to which adverse-selection results generalize across insurance settings remains an important qualification.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic discrete-choice methods made forward-looking decisions empirically tractable across labour, industrial organization and public economics.
assessment.attribution: Rust is foundational, while Keane and Eckstein made major contributions to structural estimation and applications.
assessment.maturity: The framework is long established and remains a core tool of applied structural work.
uncertainties: Credit for the wider dynamic structural-estimation tradition is necessarily broader than three researchers.
